Introduction to the CAT Syllabus 2025
IIMs do not provide any ofﬁcial syllabus to prepare for the Common Admission Test
(CAT). However, based on data collated from the past years’ papers, a brief overview
of the syllabus can be collated to start your CAT preparations systematically.
CAT syllabus 2025 is divided into three sections:
Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC)
Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR)
Quantitative Aptitude (QA)
The VARC section of CAT 2025 focuses on school-level English, including reading
comprehension, odd one out, para completion, etc. Similarly, the QA section covers
the syllabus of middle-school mathematics. The major topics covered are algebra,
arithmetic, modern maths, geometry, number system, etc. Last but not least, the
DILR section of CAT 2025 is the only section that candidates are unfamiliar with as it
is not covered in school or college syllabi for most. It focuses on compiling data
provided based on charts, graphs, and diagrams provided.

CAT VARC Syllabus 2025
The VARC section is the ﬁrst section of the exam which must be completed in 40
minutes. The Reading Comprehension part of the section dominates with
approximately 70% weightage of the total score of this section. Given below are the
topics that should be covered in the CAT VARC syllabus 2025:
For the past few years, the section has focused on majorly 5 types of questions:
1. Summary Questions
Small passage (80-100 words) with 4 options
The objective is to ﬁnd the best summary of the passage.
In these types of questions, the key is usually to ﬁnd the options that do not
contradict the passage in any manner or go beyond the scope of the discussion.
Once you are able to eliminate the other options, the right answer will emerge.
2. Jumbled Paragraph Questions
These are usually TITA, which means that there is no margin for error. In these types of
questions, there are 4-5 sentences given out of order. Together they form a paragraph,
and the aspirant has to ﬁnd the order which best suits the group of sentences. To
answer these kinds of questions, the ﬁrst thing that each aspirant needs to do is
identify the ﬁrst and last sentence of the paragraph.
This is usually quite easy since the ﬁrst sentence introduces a topic while the last
sentence makes some kind of judgment or conclusion.
Following this, the ﬁrst sentence should lead to the second sentence, and so on and
so forth.
3. Odd Sentence in Paragraph Jumbles
Like jumbled paragraph questions, it has also been a TITA question for the past 3-4
years.

The objective is to identify the sentence which does not match the theme established
in the rest of the paragraph.
These questions may be easy or difﬁcult, depending on how they are presented.
In easy questions, the sentence will talk about something completely different from
the theme of the rest of the passage.
In difﬁcult questions, the sentence will be on the same topic as the rest of the passage
but will slightly differ in terms of the opinion being offered or the theme being set. It is
also possible for the sentence to introduce a topic within the theme which is not
pursued further.
4. Para-completion
Para-completion is nothing more than a comprehension test. It only requires you to
add a missing line to a paragraph. Some key aspects to keep in mind while solving
such questions are: Determine the topic of the paragraph and attempt to summarize
the action in the paragraph in your own words.
Identify the point in the author's argument that we are left within the paragraph.
Continue your train of thinking rather than focusing on speciﬁc words or phrases.
Last but not least, stay away from extreme answer options.
5. Reading Comprehension
The Reading Comprehension section consists of questions based on passages
provided. The questions are generally a mix of fact-based and inferential questions. For
the past few years, CAT has focused on asking questions that are more inference-
based. These questions demand a deeper and more nuanced understanding of the
information given. They are slightly trickier since the aspirant has to deduce the tone
and theme of the author before answering these questions.
The fact-based questions, as the name suggests, demand answers on the basis of
facts mentioned in the passage. They are usually easier to attempt.
The CAT 2024 RC section was structured in the same manner as the CAT 2023 paper
regarding the types of questions, which made the section more complex in terms of
the level of difﬁculty. The same can be expected from CAT 2025.

The second section of the CAT exam, the DILR section, is the most undeﬁned as
compared to the other sections in the CAT Exam Syllabus. The three subsections of
the DILR section in the CAT syllabus 2025 is Data Interpretation (DI): Data will be
presented in the form of a graph, chart, or another form of visualization, and you will be
required to solve the questions given based on the information given. Logical
Reasoning (LR): Here, you may be given information in a non-structured manner, and
you may be required to structure it and derive the outcome to solve the questions
given. Arrangement (AR): Here, you may be given information in the form of conditions,
and you may be required to organize it and answer the given questions. Given below
are the major topics of the CAT DILR syllabus-
The number of questions in the DI, LR and AR sub-sections are generally distributed in
the ratio 1 : 2 : 1 respectively, which means that the students who are more comfortable
in one of the sub-sections can still clear the cut-off if they attempt that part of the CAT
2025 Paper well.

CAT DILR Syllabus 2025

However, the CAT DILR Section has been changing slightly in recent years. The
questions are a combination of DI and LR rather than the regimented, separate DI and
LR questions that were tested earlier. DILR was the trickiest section for aspirants in CAT
2016, CAT 2017, and CAT 2020, but the difﬁculty level was reduced in CAT 2018, CAT 2019
and CAT 2021. In CAT 2022, the DILR section was still moderate. However, the difficulty
level increased in CAT 2023. One of the reasons for this difﬁculty is the unpredictability
of the sections in terms of where the sets could be taken from. The CAT syllabus 2025
for the DILR section is:
1. Data Interpretation (DI)
The DI section of the CAT Syllabus consists of Caselets and Tables. These caselets have
data in the form of Bar graphs, Pie charts, Lines graphs, Combination graphs, and other
different diagrams. In this section of the CAT Exam Syllabus, the aspirants will be asked
to solve questions that are posed based on the data given in the above formats. In
order to solve these questions, the data has to be structured in the most intuitive
manner so that the questions can be solved. In certain questions, there will be variables
that have to be left untouched since they may be provided in the questions. The only
way to prepare for this section in the CAT exam is to solve as many problems as
possible and go through the previous years’ CAT Exam Papers.
2. Logical Reasoning (LR)
The topics for Logical Reasoning in the CAT syllabus over the years consist of Numbers
and Sequences, Set Theory, Games and Tournaments, Grid/Matrix, Cubes/Cuboids,
Letter/Number Coding, Binary Logic, Different diagrams number & logic-based, Route
based and Time Table of Trains & Flights. The questions are usually arranged with a
combination of the other topics. The number of topics for Logical Reasoning is quite
numerous, and the combination can lead to very tricky sets. This can be one of the
reasons that CAT 2015, CAT 2016 and CAT 2023 were considered to have difﬁcult DILR
sections. The reasoning topics can lead to very complicated sets when combined with
each other. The major concern with solving LR questions is not to solve them but to
solve them as expeditiously as possible.
3. Arrangement (AR)
The topics for Analytical Reasoning in the CAT syllabus across the years consist of
Matrix Arrangement, Linear Arrangement, Family Tree, Logical Sequence, Selection,
Grouping, Teams, and Committees. In this section of the CAT syllabus, candidates will
be asked to organize the given information and answer the given questions.

CAT Quant Syllabus 2025
Arithmetic: This topic covers the maximum number of questions in most of the
CAT Exams and is a topic that all students should prepare for. 
Algebra: This topic has the second-highest weightage in terms of the questions
asked in the CAT Exam.
Number System: These are topics that are regularly tested in the CAT Exam and
every aspirant should be clear about the basics of the topics to not lose out on
easy marks.
Geometry: This is another regularly tested topic that consists of 3D figures,
Coordinate Geometry, Mensuration, etc. Having a basic knowledge of the topic
will allow aspirants to attempt at least a few questions from the topic in the CAT
2025 Exam.
Modern Maths: It has been observed in the previous years that the number of
questions from modern maths has started increasing. There are prominently 2-3
questions asked from topics including P & C, probability, etc.

Here are a few tips for each of the topics- Arithmetic is also fairly basic and should be
easy to prepare for. Most of the topics in Arithmetic are of Class X level and the only
trick is to solve them as fast as possible.
Alignments and mixes are similar to sequences and mixes in the sense that they are
occasionally tested in CAT. It is fairly easy to solve problems of this type with the right
guidance.

Algebra may be used in conjunction with other topics or may be tested in CAT 2025.
Sequence and Series is a topic that is occasionally tested in CAT and regularly in other
MBA Entrance Exams. With practice, the questions in this topic can be easily solved.
Geometry has several rules, and ﬁnding the most important geometry rules would
allow the aspirant to solve these problems as fast as possible.
Modern mathematics is reasonably easy to prepare for since the number of questions
is limited and the formulae to be learned are fairly straightforward.
